To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
myxoma viruses isolated from the European rabbit (in Portugal) over the last 50 years are genetically stable, and that the live attenuated vaccine is genetically different from virulent strains.

(i) the genetic stability of myxo virus over the past decades is supported by the high degree of sequence identity between the analysed field strains and (ii) the attenuated phenotype of the MAV vaccine strain could be due to major genomic changes that were not detectable in the regions analysed in this study.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution of the myxomatosis pathogen in its new host.
the evolution of myxoma viruses in their new host and the genetic changes underlying the attenuation of the live vaccine strain.
the molecular epidemiology of the European rabbit myxomatosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
myxoma virus has not changed substantially over the past five to seven decades.
myxoma virus is genetically stable and the genetic basis of its evolution in the new host remains elusive.
the genetic changes underlying myxo-virus evolution in rabbits have not been detected in the sequenced regions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the genetic stability of myxo virus over the past 50 years is a result of the fact that the virus has been kept in the laboratory, where it is passaged in a single cell type (rabbit kidney cells), and where it has not been subjected to the evolutionary pressures exerted by the natural host.
genetic changes in the field strains are limited, while the vaccine strain has been subjected to major changes.
the myxoma virus has a stable genome, which is only slightly altered in its virulent strains.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genome regions M009L, M014L/M15L, M022L and/or M036L may be involved in virulence.

the genetic stability of myxo virus over the past decades, as well as the high genetic similarity between field and vaccine strains, is a major obstacle for the genetic characterisations of myxoma viruses.
a complete genome analysis is required to study the genetic changes underlying myxo-virus evolution in the European rabbit.
